Cc: BrightStack Ops <ops@brightstack.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spike + 5xx surge — impacting inference on our prod fleet

Kimberly, team —

We started seeing a sustained p99 latency increase and a spike in 5xx error rate around 08:40 PT this morning. Our application is timing out for a portion of traffic and throughput has dropped ~25% compared to last week. Attaching a short screenshot and the top-line metrics for the past 90 minutes.

Key symptoms:
- p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.2s between 08:40–09:00
- 5xx rate rose from 0.2% to 2.4% concurrently
- Throughput (requests/s) decreased by ~25% under same customer traffic profile

We are on Redwood hosted inference (model pinned v3.2) and saw a corresponding jump in backend queueing and reject rates in our sidecar. Can someone triage immediately? This is customer-impacting.

Attachments: incident_metrics_2028-04-18.png

Thanks,
Michelle Park
CTO, BrightStack
michelle@brightstack.com

Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike + 5xx surge — initial triage notes

Initial triage notes (10:02 PT):

Observations:
- KV store for tenant brightstack-prod showed a ~4x increase in occupancy and a correlated series of eviction waves starting at 08:38:51.
- Eviction waves coincide with a handful of very large key insertions (~10–100x usual key size) from a small subset of API keys — looks like a misbehaving client pattern interleaving large context writes + frequent reads.
- Batching lanes experienced slot exhaustion: steady-state batch formation delayed (batch assembly timeout increased), producing longer tail latencies and some internal rate-limits triggering 429/5xx cascades.
- Evidence of head-of-line blocking: when a hot key was being serviced in the same lane, other requests in that lane queued behind it and experienced amplified latency.

Actions taken (immediate):
- Enabled per-tenant emergency bypass lane for brightstack-prod to route new requests to a fast-path that avoids large-prefetch code path (mitigates HOL blocking for small requests).
- Temporarily reduced prefetch concurrency from 8 -> 3 for brightstack-prod to lower simultaneous KV insert pressure.
- Increased soft eviction threshold at the runtime layer for brightstack-prod to reduce eviction churn.

Attachments uploaded: kv_dump_2028-04-18.json (kv store sample), diagnostic logs excerpt (inline snippet).

Inline log snippet:
-----BEGIN LOG EXCERPT-----
2028-04-18T08:39:50Z tenant=brightstack-prod eviction_triggered keys=342 delta_mb=+128
2028-04-18T08:39:51Z tenant=brightstack-prod batch_lane=3 slot_alloc_failures=12
2028-04-18T08:40:12Z tenant=brightstack-prod request_id=abc123 tail_latency_ms=1214 status=500
2028-04-18T08:40:25Z tenant=brightstack-prod prefetch_concurrency=8 -> 3 (emergency)
-----END LOG EXCERPT-----

Next steps:
- Continue monitoring for stabilization (baseline p99 and 5xx).
- If we see improvement in 10–20 minutes, we'll keep the emergency bypass and schedule a configuration rollback path and a more targeted change to key-size limits and per-key rate limiting.
- If the bypass causes regressions, we'll roll back immediately and proceed with a staged capacity increase on Dedicated pools as contingency.

I'll push a short note to the Grafana panel and update the JIRA ticket.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.example

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Latency spike + 5xx surge — mitigation and customer comms

Thanks Marcus — good quick work. Observed impact and comms plan:

Immediate mitigation summary (already applied):
- Emergency bypass lane enabled (reduces HOL blocking for small/latency-sensitive requests).
- Prefetch concurrency throttle applied (reduces eviction storms).
- Soft eviction threshold increased (reduces churn).

Customer-facing comms:
- Kimberly: propose we send BrightStack a one-paragraph incident update now with ETA for stabilization ("engineering applied emergency mitigations; we're monitoring and will follow up with a timeline and root cause within X hours").
- If BrightStack asks for credits, I'll propose a short-term credit (X% for impacted window) and escalate for exec sign-off.

Longer-term remediation items (post-incident):
- Add per-key size and write-rate limits at the tenant layer to prevent large-insert storms.
- Add adaptive batching lane isolation: detect heavy keys and route them to isolated lanes to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Update onboarding docs for BrightStack to call out recommended SDK write patterns and limits.

I'll prepare a short RCA template and a follow-up plan once we stabilize.

Rishi
Director, Product Ops
rishi@redwood.example

Team & BrightStack execs —

Quick situational brief:
- Impact window: 08:38–09:05 PT; primary symptoms were p99 latency and ~2% 5xx; throughput drop ~25%.
- Root cause (preliminary): KV occupancy and key-size insertion storm causing eviction waves + batch-lane slot exhaustion which produced HOL blocking for latency-sensitive requests.
- Immediate mitigations applied: emergency bypass lane, lowered prefetch concurrency, raised soft eviction threshold.
- Current status: steady improvement observed; p99 trending back toward baseline, 5xx reduced to ~0.3% as of 15:20 PT.

Requested from leadership:
1) Executive approval to offer BrightStack a goodwill credit for the impacted window (recommendation: 20% credit for April 18 window).
2) Approval to prioritize the adaptive lane isolation change on the SRE roadmap (2-week sprint).
3) Exec presence for 11:00 PT sync if leadership from BrightStack would like a live briefing (Kim — you proposed 11:00 earlier; please confirm).

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: continue monitoring and post a stabilization confirmation in JIRA (JIRA-OPS-9721).
- Rishi: draft customer incident update and credit proposal.
- Kimberly: confirm 11:00 PT sync and lead customer comms.
- Prioy (sic): prepare deployment playbook for lane-isolation change and runbook tests.

I'll be available on the 11:00 PT bridge. Please confirm approvals and any changes to the recommended credit.

—
